sections.h2: Your options for a quick Bartlett sale
sections.html:
Three paths are open: an agent, a sale handled on your own, or a cash offer for the house as it stands. Speed is the selling point of cash, because the buyer needs no loan and no appraisal. A traditional listing can still net more if the house shows well and your schedule is flexible.

  • Agent listing: best shot at a top price, though you will deal with repair requests, open houses and the buyer's loan approval.
  • By owner: the commission stays in your pocket, while pricing, paperwork and disclosure fall on you.
  • Cash purchase: the house goes as it stands, on a short clock, without repairs or showings.

Every route ends at the same three stops in Bartlett and Shelby County: a city code check, a tax payoff and a deed filed with the Shelby County Register. A cash sale also skips cleaning out the house for showings, fixing what an inspector flags and carrying the mortgage while a buyer's loan is approved.

Bartlett sits in Shelby County and had 56,416 residents on July 1, 2025, a drop of 2.4 percent from the April 2020 base of 57,792. Most homes are owner occupied (85.6 percent), and the median owned home is worth $310,400. Median gross rent is $1,638, and monthly owner costs run $1,775 with a mortgage and $639 without. With 91.4 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier, the neighborhood is settled, so buyers tend to weigh condition against price.

sections.h2: Code enforcement before a house sale
sections.html:
Bartlett's Code Compliance department checks sidewalks and storm inlets when it learns a house is for sale. Staff mark any sidewalk or inlet that needs replacement or repair.

The Code Enforcement Department is at 6382 Stage Road, 901-385-6425, with hours of 8 to 5, Monday to Friday. It handles permits, plan review and inspections, and it also does MLGW service turn-on inspections. Permits are required for fences, decks, detached buildings, swimming pools of 24 inches or deeper, additions, siding, window replacement, concrete patios and driveway extensions. Water heater, HVAC and electrical work must be pulled by a contractor who holds the state license for that trade.

Deal with older unpermitted work before the buyer's inspector spots it. A call to the department tells you if a fence, deck or addition has a permit on file.

sections.h2: How are Bartlett house taxes billed?
sections.html:
Bartlett property carries a city bill and a separate county bill. The city mails its bills before December 1, payable through February 28, and the bill is late starting March 1. Shelby County collects prior years' city taxes.

Bartlett and Shelby County tax and recording charges
ChargeAmount or due date
County tax dueFirst Monday of October, payable through the last day of February
City of Bartlett billsMailed before December 1, payable through February 28
Late interest1.5% of base tax on March 1, then monthly
State transfer tax$0.37 for each $100 of price or value
Deed recording$12.00 for up to 2 pages, $5.00 each added page
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 after first $2,000

The city emails a tax file to the major mortgage companies. If you have a mortgage, forward any notice you receive to your lender anyway.

sections.h2: Who to call about Bartlett property taxes
sections.html:
Appraisal changes and ownership updates go through the Shelby County Assessor, 1075 Mullins Station Road in Memphis, 901-222-7001. The Shelby County Trustee, 157 Poplar Ave., 901-222-0200, collects the county tax and takes delinquent city tax payments on weekdays until 4:30 p.m.

The county offers some payment flexibility. A Quarterly Pay program lets qualifying owners 65 or older on a fixed income pay county tax on October 31, January 31, April 30 and July 31. Call 901-222-0200 for the current application window. The trustee also accepts partial payments, with no interest if the bill is paid in full by the deadline, and offers ManagedPay monthly plans, though ManagedPay does not stop interest from accruing. The trustee also supplies city tax relief and tax freeze forms for older owners.

Deeds for Bartlett houses are recorded with the Shelby County Register of Deeds, main office at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Building W-3, Memphis, TN 38134. Recording takes about one business day from receipt, and a digital copy appears on the Register's website.

A taxable deed must identify grantor and grantee and include an affidavit of value, a derivation clause, the property address, who owns the parcel and who answers for its taxes, the ward, block and parcel number, the preparer's contact details, and a valid acknowledgment. Taxable deeds pay $0.37 per $100. Deeds between divorcing spouses, deeds that carry out a will, and transfers into or out of a revocable living trust are exempt under T.C.A. 67-4-409.

Before the closing office files anything, check that names on the deed match your title records and that every item above is filled in. A missing affidavit or acknowledgment can delay recording and push back the date the buyer gets the keys. A title or closing office usually prepares the deed, but you should still read it before you sign.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Bartlett
sections.html:
Begin with your newest city and county tax bills plus permit papers for any fence, deck or addition. Call Code Enforcement early so a missing permit or a damaged sidewalk does not surprise you late in the sale. Then ask the Shelby County Trustee what you owe, because back taxes come out of the sale money.

A cash buyer brings no lender and no appraisal, so title work sets the closing date. A listing moves at the buyer's lender's pace. On closing day you sign the deed, the transfer tax is paid, and the Register records it, usually within one business day. Ask the closing office to send you the recorded copy.

Owed taxes and late interest are settled from your proceeds, so no separate check is needed. Take a photo ID, keys, garage openers and permit paperwork. Disclose known defects before you sign.

Buyers touring Bartlett tend to ask about parks and civic facilities. The Bartlett Recreation Center is a 55,000 square foot building that opened in August 2000. The Bartlett Senior Center sits across from Bartlett High School and is open to anyone 50 or older with a membership. The Performing Arts and Conference Center at 3663 Appling Road faces the Bartlett Police Station and Appling Middle School. Bartlett City Schools runs the public schools. Naming these places in your listing or a seller's note helps an out of town buyer picture the neighborhood.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Bartlett house be sold?
faqs.a: If title is clear, a cash sale can close within days. A listing runs on the buyer's lender schedule, and a deed takes about one business day to record at the Shelby County Register.

faqs.q: Is there a city inspection when a Bartlett house goes on the market?
faqs.a: Code Compliance checks and marks sidewalks and storm inlets needing repair when it is notified of a house for sale. Code Enforcement, 901-385-6425, can tell you what applies to your lot.

faqs.q: When are Bartlett city property taxes due?
faqs.a: City bills are mailed before December 1 and are payable through February 28, with delinquency starting March 1. Shelby County collects prior year city taxes.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax comes with a Bartlett sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of price or value, whichever is greater. The Shelby County Register collects it with the deed.
Bartlett City Schools, formed after a July 16, 2013 referendum and operating since fall 2014 with the 11 school buildings inside the city limits.
